title: EcoBench load-fidelity validation sandbox and customer acceptance checklist
creator: Diego Martínez
description: Create a reproducible, tenant-aware load testing sandbox (EcoBench) and a customer-facing acceptance checklist to validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior. The goal is to deliver a test harness and documented methodology customers and SREs can run to reproduce capacity measurements used in contracts.
hypothesis: If we provide a deterministic, tenant-mixer driven harness with telemetry-aligned metrics and a concise acceptance checklist, customers will be able to independently validate committed throughput and observe autoscaler behavior under controlled bursts, reducing disputes and onboarding time.
scope: Build harness components (EcoBench CLI, PulseMixer workload composer, KV priming utility). Define benchmark methodology (profiles, seeds, quantiles) and a customer acceptance test plan. Exclude multi-region failover scenarios (follow-up epic).
success_metrics: Reproducible p99 and p99.9 within ±7% across 3 repeated runs
Autoscaler triggers at configured thresholds within 60s and stabilizes within policy window
Customer acceptance checklist completed by pilot customer within 2 hours
End-to-end test produces signed artifact for contract evidence (csv + dashboard link)
runbook_steps: 1) Install EcoBench CLI and authenticate to a dedicated test tenant
2) Load model variant and pin sequence length profile matching customer SLA
3) Use PulseMixer to create a tenant mix profile (idle fraction, bursty tenants, sustained tenants)
4) Prime KV cache using KVCache-Priming utility with representative prefix/prompt set
5) Ramp to steady-state QPS using ramp profile (3m ramp, 20m sustain), collect baseline latencies
6) Inject microbursts and step-load increases to exercise autoscaler policies, record scale events
7) Run three full iterations (A/B/C) with identical seeds and collect quantile summaries
8) Produce evidence bundle: raw traces, aggregated quantiles, autoscaler event log, and EcoBench manifest
9) Run customer acceptance checklist and sign off on evidence bundle
data_collection: Telemetry is collected via the standard runtime tracing hooks. EcoBench attaches a run_id prefix (ecobench-<key>) to all requests and emits: latency_ms, tokens_out, model_variant, node_id, cache_hit (bool), tenant_id_tag, autoscaler_event_id. Aggregation scripts produce p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 and tail-lift charts. Artifacts are uploaded to the contract S3 bucket with immutable names.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence bundle contains 3 run artifacts and an aggregated summary CSV
P99 latency meets contractual bound for the selected model variant under the tested tenant mix
Autoscaler behaved as configured: scale-up events within 60s of threshold breach and no oscillation beyond configured cooldown
No dropped requests or internal 5xx rate > 0.1% during sustain period
Customer-run checklist executed and recorded by Support engineer (notes + timestamp)
dependencies: ENG-410002 (runtime trace enrichment for tenant tags)
risks: Noise from co-located tenants if test cluster not fully isolated
Model variant changes between runs invalidating comparisons
Insufficient KV priming leads to non-representative latency profiles
mitigations: Reserve isolated test fleet for certification runs
Freeze model-serving image for the duration of benchmark runs and record hash
Provide deterministic KV priming seeds and measure priming coverage before test start
next_steps: Prototype PulseMixer and validate deterministic seeding (due 2026-02-20)
Demo run with internal SRE and capture evidence (due 2026-02-28)
Iterate checklist with Support and Legal to finalize contract artifact format (due 2026-03-15)
Pilot with 1 anchor customer for signoff (due 2026-03-31)
